label: Street's alien-investigator reply assumes shared judgments about epistemic reasons
paraphrase: In replying to the objection that the Darwinian dilemma threatens antirealism because the antirealist relies on evolution-influenced substantive judgments about practical reasons, Street argues that an alien investigator with different practical evaluative judgments could reach the same antirealist view from the same considerations, and assumes for the sake of argument that this investigator shares our judgments about epistemic reasons. She says this assumption is complicated by her view that the dilemma extends to realism about epistemic reasons and leaves that complication undiscussed.
